# Incorrect diameter of the white dot inside the target:

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.29.18.png|width=186,height=187!

2. The incorrect transition of the target. It appears via scaling from top-left corner instead of the centre of the target:

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.30.08.png|width=190,height=386!

3. Dots of the dotted line are too long, they’re supposed to be circular.

4. Please, never animate text labels and tooltip targets this way:

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.35.24.png|width=190,height=114!

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.35.33.png|width=201,height=137!

The tooltip must appear as a whole element together with its text label inside. Please find a description of the correct tooltip transition in the [UI kit|https://www.figma.com/file/QcjHW7d0EaAa8QOASWK2L5/Rider-UI-Kit?type=design&node-id=36353%3A19710&mode=design&t=u4csgHy8RfJPaz9i-1].

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 16.38.03.png|width=525,height=360!



5. A tooltip should be [realigned|https://www.figma.com/file/1TPfCQUmG4BJ4hVVxuXfsE/Taras-Sandbox?type=design&node-id=19981%3A134356&mode=design&t=NiMB0z0XTC0ylUFY-1] so that it isn’t covered by the pin. If it’s impossible, it should at least be displayed over the tooltip.

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.36.49.png|width=234,height=180!

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.42.33.png|width=523,height=159!

6. When a pin is moved to the recommended point, we should remove the initial point and the tooltip. The white dot diameter should also be fixed here:

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.36.26.png|width=378,height=242!

7. Just in case, this small green pin is only needed if the pickup location was input manually (an order for someone else). In the majority of cases, there should be a standard “my current location“ blue dot instead.

!Screenshot 2023-07-12 at 15.48.42.png|width=433,height=403!

8. Also, we’re missing the message “You’re currently in a no-car zone. This is the nearest available road stop.“ It should be displayed as a snackbar (old version) or as a subtitle (new version, AB test in progress).

                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.state='finished'

  1
            ),
            COUNT_of_fraud_orders AS (
SELECT

  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
JOIN drivers_age as da ON (ot.driver_id = da.driver_id)
  WHERE
    etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
      AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
      AND ot.state = 'finished'
      AND ot.price_review_status = 'ok'
      AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price
      AND co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                            AND (
(etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))

OR
(DATEDIFF(day,da.min_fecha, CURRENT_DATE) < 15 AND oc.pickup_duration <= 20)
)  
    GROUP BY
      1
            )
            -- Creamos nueva sub-tabla
            , SELECT_cash_out as (
            SELECT 
            etl.city_id || ':' || etl.order_id AS KEY,
            1 AS fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id

LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN COUNT_of_orders AS x ON x.driver_id = ot.driver_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
LEFT JOIN COUNT_of_fraud_orders AS y ON y.driver_id = ot.driver_id
JOIN drivers_age as da ON (ot.driver_id = da.driver_id)
WHERE
  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'

                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price
  AND ot.price_review_status = 'ok'
  AND ot.city_id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
                      AND (
(etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))
OR  
(etl.country_code = 'ng' AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 100 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30) AND ROUND(etl.rider_disCOUNT*1.00/etl.partner_price,2) >= 0.45)
OR 
(DATEDIFF(day,da.min_fecha, CURRENT_DATE) < 15 AND oc.pickup_duration <= 20)
)  
GROUP BY
  1,
  y.COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
  x.COUNT_of_inapp_orders,
  y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders,
  x.COUNT_of_cash_orders
HAVING
  ((y.COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders >= 4
    AND y.COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.COUNT_of_inapp_orders, 0)>= 0.5)
    OR (y.COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders >= 5
      AND y.COUNT_of_inapp_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.COUNT_of_inapp_orders, 0)>= 0.4))
  OR
            ((y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 4
    AND y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.COUNT_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.5)
    OR
            (y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 6
      AND y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.COUNT_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.4))
              OR
        (y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 10
      AND y.COUNT_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.COUNT_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.3)
            )
      -- Subquery to get the finished orders FROM the last 8 days with the driver_acceptance lat AND lng
      , orders as (
      SELECT etv.company_order__country as country, etv.company_order__city_id as city_id, etv.company_order__user_id as user_id, etv.company_order_try__driver_id as driver_id
      , etv.company_order__id as order_id, etv.company_order__lat as rider_lat, etv.company_order__lng as rider_lng 
      , etv.driver_accepted_lat, etv.driver_accepted_lng
      , etv.company_order__campaign_code as campaign_code, etv.company_order__state as order_sate
      , CASE WHEN (driver_accepted_lat = company_order__lat AND driver_accepted_lng = company_order__lng AND company_order__campaign_code is not null AND etv.company_order__state = 'finished') then true else false end as is_fraud_order       
      FROM ng_public_spark.etl_search_denormalized_view as etv 
      WHERE true 
        AND etv.created_date >= dateadd(day,-8,current_date)
        AND etv.company_order__state = 'finished'
      )
      --- The following section has the purpose to add the profiling thas corresponds to rides where te gps when the ride was created is the same of the driver when it accepted the ride ---
      -- Subquery with the stats of the drivers regarding fraud orders AND total orders over the last 8 days 
      , drivers_stats as (
      SELECT driver_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) as total_events
      , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_fraud_order = true then order_id end) as fraud_events
      FROM orders as o 
      WHERE true
      group by 1 
      )
      -- Subquery to select the orders from the drivers that had 4 or more fraud orders or more than 20% of their orders are considered fraud based on the gps
      , fraud_gps_orders as (
      SELECT DISTINCT o.city_id || ':' || o.order_id as key, 1 as fraud_campaign_code_cash_out 
      FROM orders as o
      JOIN drivers_stats as ds 
        ON (o.driver_id = ds.driver_id)
      WHERE is_fraud_order = true 
        AND (fraud_events >= 4 or (cast(fraud_events as double)/cast(total_events as double)) >= 0.2)
        AND (cast(fraud_events as double)/cast(total_events as double)) >= 0.1
        AND o.city_id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
      )
      -- we combine the profiles AND SELECT all the selected orders 
      , all_selected as (
      SELECT *
      FROM fraud_gps_orders
      UNION all 
      SELECT *
      FROM select_cash_out
      )
      SELECT DISTINCT *
      FROM all_selected
      -- (1900 aprox original --> 3384 with new profile (+1484) --> 3191 no duplicates (+1291) --> 2411 with at least 10% (+511) --> 2858 with at least 4 fraud gps orders (+958))

For this result set the read set from the fee table will exceed 1 million this week. It’s not feasible to migrate completely to RH v2 in a week even so we need a solution and quickly.

My proposal is to create a task after each fee calculation and make a new cron to handle those tasks (calculate the balance). Then we can remove the fee table scan from the query. let’s start with the lag.

The data appears on s3 almost immediately thanks to s3 sink connector. You can track consumer lag [here|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/8LW1Yd8ik/kafka-lag-exporter?orgId=1&viewPanel=82&refresh=1m].  This part is a matter of minutes max if everything is fine. But to make this data useful\queryable by presto and spark a few more steps are required. There is spark cron job that triggered hourly and processes X-1 hour of data. So the end data is available in presto\spark in 1h after being pushed to Kafka.

So the full answer would really depend on what you need is.

What is the use case?

What is inside SNS message?

Are you going to use Presto to read the data?

How would the load structured (amount of reads\writes per day, number o bytes per read\write)?

Ok, so let’s start with my use case. An ML model called colt-traffic does an expensive preprocessing step (right before training the model) of map matching 40 days of tracking data to the latest OSM map.

We want to eliminate this process and use the {{routing-edges-event}} SNS topic, which contains real-time matched tracking points. As you can see in this [chart|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/000000010/aws-sns?orgId=1&var-Datasource=CloudWatch&var-region=eu-central-1&var-topic=routing-edges-event&from=now-24h&to=now&refresh=1m], there are a maximum of 16K messages every 5 minutes with an average size of 51 KiB each.

After preprocessing it (we need another structure), we want to export that data to S3 and have it ready for the training step (if it’s better, we can query it directly from Presto instead of S3). For now, we need to keep only 40 days of history at most. 

In the future, we would want to have this data with the minimum lag possible to view the traffic in almost real-time, but for now, we are exploring all our options.

You make a good point, unfortunately Leapsome does a silly thing with averages and adds all questions to the weight, regardless of scale, etc.

That being said, you should ignore what Leapsome returns as average score, but rather look at the relevant performance question. For example, for annual performance review, both you and your manager needed to add an “Overall Performance Score”. This is your rating, your manager rated “Often excellent (4/5)” which means that this is your rating, not the average shown by Leapsome.

For example, this year during salary review, managers had also the Leapsome rating as information along with other employee details. If you would have been eligible, your manager would have seen Performance rating : Often Excellent.

Managers should also be aware of this understanding, but of course, in your next 121 you can raise this and highlight the fact that Leapsome shows irelevant averages and that your performance review shows the overall performance rating.

Hope this clarifies!

Hi [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b] as discussed below is the summary of our understanding of the situation and recommendation:

* Currently vehicles in the categories “Bolt” and “XL” are eligible for the “Assist” category. 
* Not all vehicles in the “Bolt” category can accommodate wheelchairs and for this reason OPS would like only allow vehicles in the category “XL” to be eligible for the “Assist” category with the aim of improving this service.
* The TVDE law establishes obligations in relation to passengers with reduced mobility (article 6).
* In particular, the law establishes that electronic platforms must provide a way to individuals with reduced mobility to have a ride on a vehicle capable of accommodating them and their wheelchair.
* All the vehicles in the “XL” category can accommodate wheelchairs, but not all the vehicles in the “Bolt” category can. 
* Therefore, having only “XL” vehicles eligible for “Assist” category would therefore appear not to be against the TVDE law requirements.
* However, *we recommend that the following measures are further implement to ensure compliance with TVDE law*:
** Information is provided directly in the Bolt app, in a clear way (for instance under a little ‘i' (for information / details) next to the 'Assist’ category logo / offer in the app) to clarify that the +“Assist” category offers “XL” vehicles to ensure capacity to transport extra means of locomotion [hence why pricing is same as “XL”category+
** Additional information should be given - in the FAQ for instance - to further clarify that:
*** the eligibility for “Assist” is only for “XL” vehicles in order to ensure that the rider always travels in a larger vehicle that is capable of transporting his/her means of locomotion (this is to ensure compliance with article 6.1 of TVDE law);
*** the price calculation for “Assist” is exactly the same as for the “XL” category (this is to ensure compliance with article 6.4 of TVDE law)

While investigating this ticket, we realised that the {{last_login}} we currently store for users is inconsistent and not completely reliable for the archival of users. (also, the wording for it is not very descriptive: is the the time the user went through the login flow? the last time the user used the app?).

In designing a correct solution for this, it would be good to formally establish what actions should make a user be considered 'active' from the point of view of user archival. Should the bare action of opening the app be enough for the user to be active, or should he/she/it need to order a ride, modify their profile, etc?

Also, from a data retention point of view: we only archive users when somebody tries to log in using that phone number. That means that users that uninstall the app and never try to login again are never archived. Is this a correct behaviour?

_All of these questions will need to be answered, then we can design a proper solution (this will be done in a future task). At first glance, it seems we need to create a new field where we can track the last user action (once we define what exactly is a user action)._

h2. *Data insights*

*I lost a personal item*

* Spain and Germany have market-specific instructions for contacting fleet owners if drivers don’t respond. Both markets have one of the highest handling time (ES - 9.9 min; DE - 9.1 min). For both markets, CSAT and first SSAT are a bit below the average, which may indicate that even the addition of this market-specific step doesn’t result in a better user satisfaction. 
** Additionally, in Spain there’s a significant difference in AHT between Bolt and Majorel agents (Majorel - 8.9, Bolt - 25.1 🤯). The volumes handled by Bolt agents are way smaller than the ones handled by Majorel (1,869 vs. 113). Perhaps in-house agents deal mostly with cases escalated by Majorel and they further escalate them to Ops team?
** I will check with TLs responsible for these markets if they know whether this step actually helps to retrieve customer’s item. 
** If not, then we should remove these instructions.
** If yes, we can consider implementing this step in other markets which have fleet owners.
* Norway also has quite high AHT (8.9) and there are also market-specific instructions (CS should escalate to OPS who contact the FO). As opposed to Spain and Germany, Norway is more interesting though because although the first SSAT is low, CSAT is the third highest (86%).
** Same comment as for the previous point - I’ll check with the TL about this.
* Ireland (no data on PA) and Belgium (100% PA in May) have the highest handling time. The volumes are not very high but it’d good to check what causes it.
* Partner markets (MX, AT, Saudi Arabia, GE, LB, HU, TN) have very low handling time, so I’d like to find out what causes it.
* As for core markets, UA (94% PA in May) and LT (52% PA in May) have lowest HT. It is very interesting because while UA has a high process adherence score, it looks like LT follows an undocumented process, so I should check what they do differently.
** In addition, CSAT in LT is 76% which is above average (same with first SSAT - also above average).
** This is definitely worth checking as perhaps there’s something we could add to the global process based on LT experience.
* HU, NO and EE have the highest CSAT. When it comes to EE, the PA is 84%. What is also worth adding is that EE has the highest first SSAT rate (71%), while AHT is quite high 7.5. High CSAT and high first SSAT for EE clearly indicates that there’s something in the way CS handles these cases that makes customers happy, so it’d be good to check that. Most of the lost item volumes are handled by Majorel, so these results are mostly driven by them.

*I lost my phone*

* In terms of AHT, France has one of the highest results (10.9). Their CSAT is among the lowest ones (46%), similar with first SSAT (24%) - both of these metrics are below an average. 
** For I lost a personal item, the results are also not the best in FR: AHT - 8.8; CSAT - 57%; 35%. PA scores are high for both issue tags.
* The three markets with market-specific instructions again have high AHT (DE - 10.8; NO - 10.4; ES - 9.9). Here again Norway CSAT (60%) and first SSAT (50%) are above the average.
* Belgium is quite interesting because for both issue tags, AHT is quite high (10 & 9.2), first SSAT is not so good (48%, 24%), yet CSAT is quite high (74%, 86%), why?
* Once again, partner markets (MX, AT, Saudi Arabia, GE, LB) have the lowest AHT. 
* As for core markets, AZ and UA have lowest AHT.

Hi Susana!

I have received information from the product team.

Those statuses reflect the fact of whether they need an agent to work on them:

* {{New}} - those are {{Active}}, {{Unassigned}} tasks - they need attention, and no one is assigned to them currently
* {{In Progress}} - those are {{Active}}, {{Assigned}} tasks - then need attention, and someone is assigned to them currently - so those tasks actively occupy the agent’s time, it can be those to which an agent is assigned and is forming a response or those in which the agent is in a phone call.
* {{Inactive}} - those are tasks which do not need attention at the moment but aren’t yet resolved. Those can be tasks, to which a response has been provided to a customer and we’re awaiting a reply (pending), or tasks put on hold.
* {{Closed}} - those are tasks which do not need attention and are resolved. (That in practice includes both {{Solved}} and {{Closed}} support cases)

Given the above, the 2 stats you’re asking about mean:

* {{Average active task age (in minutes)}} - the average age (since task creation) of a task which needs attention from an agent (it can be either assigned or unassigned).
* {{Oldest active task age (in minutes)}} - the task with the longest duration since task creation to now, which still requires attention from an agent.

* Indeed, ANPC has no jurisdiction and cannot directly impose the fines on foreign entities not having the local presence in RO. 
* Nevertheless, substantive rules (such as the ANPC orders) apply indirectly because any protection granted to consumers in Romania should be observed by ANPC, but sanctions should be imposed via the Estonian authority, through Regulation (EU) 2017/2394.  
* Obviously, we cannot exclude if ANPC will decide to overstep such boundaries and impose fine on Bolt directly, but in any case, the risk of being fined via EE authority exists. 
* Therefore, although formally ANPC does not have the jurisdiction and cannot impose the fines on Bolt Ops (since there is no Bolt Ops local presence in RO), we must obey the RO consumer laws, including those orders or legal acts issued by ANPC. Failure to do that can also affect other verticals in RO.

I’ve checked on the Swiss legal framework to come out with the following conclusions:



“- In Switzerland, e-signatures are legally recognized and governed by the *Federal Act on Electronic Signature (ZertES)* and the *Swiss Code of Obligations*.

ZertES recognise four types of electronic signatures with increasing levels of trustworthiness:

# Simple electronic signature (SES) – data in electronic form, which is attached to, or logically associated with, other data in electronic form and which aims at authenticating such data.
# Advanced electronic signature (AES) – a SES that is also:
## uniquely linked to its holder;
## capable of identifying its holder;
## created with means which the holder can use under his or her sole control; and
## linked to the associated data in such a way that any subsequent change in the data is detectable.
# Regulated electronic signature (RES) – an AES that is created by a secure electronic signature creation device under the FAES and is based on a regulated certificate.
# Qualified electronic signature (QES): – a RES that is based on a qualified certificate.

In Switzerland, a QES has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature according to the Swiss Code of Obligations *(Article 14, 2 bis)*. Thus, QES provides the highest probative value in civil proceedings. However, other types of digital signatures are also recognised and legally binding.

According to *Article 2(g)* of the ZertES, a digital certification used for a RES or QES must be issued by a certified organization that complies with the Act’s requirements and is certified by an accredited conformity assessment body. Currently, only four certificate bodies exist in Switzerland:Swisscom (Schweiz) AG, QuoVadis Trustlink Schweiz AG, SwissSign AG, and Bundesamt für Informatik und Telekommunikation BIT. *List of certified bodies in: [https://www.sas.admin.ch/sas/en/home/akkreditiertestellen/akkrstellensuchesas/pki1.html|https://www.sas.admin.ch/sas/en/home/akkreditiertestellen/akkrstellensuchesas/pki1.html|smart-link] 

Adobe Sign has no relation whatsoever with any of the ‘third party trust service providers’ mentioned in the list above, therefore, Adobe Sign is not able to provide RES or QES in Switzerland.

However, under Swiss law, the principle of freedom of form applies and contracts only require a special form when expressly prescribed by law (*Article 11* of the Swiss Code of Obligations). *Written form is specially required in certain cases.

Moreover, Swiss courts are free in their appraisal of the evidence presented to them, and there is no preference by law for certain forms of evidence (*Article 157 Swiss Civil Procedural Code*). Thus, an electronic signature cannot be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for a QES.

In conclusion, despite the fact that Adobe Sign is not able to provide RES and QES in Switzerland, unless the ‘written form’ is mandatory for the contract, we are on the safe side in the sense that Adobe Sign software meets the requirements for AES, which is recognised in Swiss regulations.

Note: since Adobe Sign with the interaction of third-party trust service providers, achieved QES standards in EU under *eIDAS* regulations, then the *paragraph 2, in article 3, Section 2(ZertES)* might be relevant to this matter as well. -”

I am happy to confirm we have an interim solution for the Cash Sweeps Transactions.
Since we still have a bit of uncertainty around the In-House Bank Accounts and how it will work. My proposal for overall solution has simplified the work we have to do on everyone's end i.e. Business and Technology.
Overall Solution Proposal is --> To only perform the Ad-Hoc Bank Transactions to replicate the "Cash Sweeps" in Bank i.e.

* Cash (Physical Bank Account) to 1410
* 2010 to Cash (Physical Bank Account)

Now the question is - What we will do with the In House Bank accounts.
Short term - Nothing.
Long term - Once we get the feel of how the transactions are happening, we could replicate the Kyriba Setup in Workday so we can then use the Virtual Accounts for different purposes envisioned by the Treasury team.Advantage of this approach is:

# We can go ahead for enabling the Cash Sweeps and help Business keep moving by enabling the Leadership having the right visibility of the Cash
# Transactions are automatically entered in Workday allowing auto-reconciliation of the transactions reducing the workload on accounting team
# Solution is divided into piece meals. This allows us to push a solution and understand the impact of it (both positive and negative).
# Allows us to refine and fine-tune future works based on the feedback received for this solution

Disadvantage of this approach is:

# We dont have the big-bang approach allowing entire solution to be in place in 1 go
# Duration of implementation can be a little longer as we are splitting solution and taking the feedback and time to understand and design the solution that works for the Business and Company

We already have a configuration in the builder - {{auto_enable_k8s_config: env[]}}. If an environment is present in the {{auto_enable_k8s_config}} array, every newly added package will be automatically assigned to all active Kubernetes clusters of the corresponding environment.

*When* {{BuildArtifacts}} *step (step responsible for kubernetes artifacts creation) is executed?*

BuildArtifacts step is added to the release pipeline if all following conditions are met:

* application config has at least one active kubernetes cluster assigned
* builder application is {{NodeServer}} (basically bolt-server)

FROM ng_public_spark.etl_rider_measurement_lib


WHERE {geo_level} = '{geo_name}'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) ftr_and_imps

JOIN 

(select 
    o.created_date as date_day,
    city.name as city,
    country.name as country,
    case when o.app_version like '%CA%' then 'android' when o.app_version like '%CI%' then 'ios' end as os,

where {geo_level}.name = '{geo_name}'
and o.created_date between date('2023-01-01') and current_timestamp()
group by 1,2,3,4
) regular_rides

on ftr_and_imps.date_day=regular_rides.date_day 
and ftr_and_imps.city=regular_rides.city

They have confirmed that they do not conduct checks on the criminal or administrative records of ride-hailing or taxi drivers, regardless of whether they are citizens of the EU or third countries. This means that drivers with previous criminal or administrative offences could obtain authorization to provide transportation services, and their licenses will not be suspended even if new offences are committed.
* To address this issue without collecting sensitive data about drivers, our goal was to establish cooperation with the LTSA. We proposed that if Bolt received a justified complaint from a passenger about a driver's behavior, we would request the LTSA to review the driver's criminal or administrative record and suspend their license if necessary. However, our cooperation proposal was rejected, and the LTSA advised us to find an internal solution to improve service quality.
* We have also received a response from Lithuanian data protection authorities (attached), which allegedly confirms that Bolt is permitted to collect such data from drivers to ensure the safe provision of transportation services. The update, update_by_query, and reindex APIs.

On the fly highlighting.

The ability to reindex from one Elasticsearch index to another, either to change mappings or analysis, or to upgrade an index to a new major version.

The ability to debug queries or aggregations by viewing the original document used at index time.

Potentially in the future, the ability to repair index corruption automatically.

Additional information regarding termination of fixed-term employment contract in Lithuania: 

* If the employment relationship under the fixed-term employment contract lasts longer than one year, the employer must notify the employee in writing about the termination of the employment contract at the end of the term no later than five working days in advance, 
* If the employment relationship under the fixed-term employment contract lasts longer than three years, no no later than ten working days in advance. After violating this duty, the employer must pay the employee wages for each day of violation of the deadline, but not more than five or ten working days.
* If the employment relationship under a fixed-term employment contract continues for more than two years, upon the termination of the employment contract at the end of the term, the employee shall be paid a severance pay equal to one month's average salary.

New comment from our local advisor:

It is not clear whether the statement that Article 43 applies only to employers is accurate. In fact, while one of the primary functions of Chapter 452 is to regulate conditions of employment (hence the relationship between employers and employees) the wording of 43(2) is wider in scope. Reference is not made specifically to employer's premises but to "to carry out in any such premises or place any examination, test or inquiry which [inspectors] may consider necessary in order to satisfy themselves that the provisions of this Act or of any regulations or orders thereunder as well any recognised conditions of employment are being observed..." Hence the question in my opinion is whether the "books, registers or other documents the keeping of which is prescribed by this Act or by any order issued under this Act..." referenced in 43(2) sub paragraph (ii) includes information which platform operators are obliged to retain in terms of Article 21 of LN268/2022. If that is the case, then I feel that the investigation obliges us to disclose any such information. For all intents, it is reminded that over a call with Mary Grace Cassar from DIER, I verbally explained that not all information was available (in particular courier earnings) since we are purely a platform which concludes service level agreements with third party fleet owners and Mary Grace Cassar mentioned we could indicate this in our response where this was relevant.

Based on [~accountid:62b1c880566f3e7b0a8f2eb7] analysis below, we cannot provide data at this stage. I’ll prepare a draft statement to send to the police is response to this matter before COB today. 

Regarding [~accountid:62b1c880566f3e7b0a8f2eb7] third point, legitimate interest (Article 6(f) GDPR) does not apply to applications made from public bodies such as the police so we are unable to rely on this.

On the whole, Bolt is heavily restricted on when we can share data with third parties. At present, the only applicable legal bases' are either consent of the data subject (which is obviously not appropriate here), or to comply with a legal obligation. This last point is why it is important we ensure the police provide the correct legal references before we provide any data.

Our duties under GDPR also do not stop here. Under GDPR we must also ensure that any data provided is relevant, proportional, and necessary to the investigation from the police. At present the police have not provided us with any rationale as to why this data is necessary for their investigation. We require the police to address all 3 of these points also before we can share data. I will address these issues in my draft response that I will provide before COB.

Due to the high profile nature of this case, our recommendation is that we ensure we are fully covered on all points before we provide data to the police.

*Info to keep handy on our UK marketing campaigns -* [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] [~accountid:5fc110f647ac91006fc4977a] 

In the context of UK marketing laws, a lottery is a form of gambling where individuals pay to participate, and the outcome is determined by chance. For a promotion or marketing campaign to be considered a lottery, it must meet three essential criteria:

# Consideration: Participants must be required to pay money or provide something of value (consideration) to enter the promotion. This can be in the form of purchasing a product or service, paying an entry fee, or making a donation.
# Chance: The outcome of the promotion must be determined by chance rather than skill. In other words, the winners are selected randomly, and participants have no control over the result.
# Prize: There must be a prize or reward for the winners. Prizes can be in the form of money, goods, services, or any other valuable items.

*Consideration*
Tagging someone in a post on social media is typically seen as a form of engagement, interaction, or communication, rather than a direct payment or exchange of value. In the UK and many other jurisdictions, the consideration element for a lottery or contest is often associated with requiring participants to pay money, provide personal information, purchase a product or service, or perform some significant action beyond the usual engagement on social media platforms. 

It’s the consideration aspect we need to be conscious of on all campaigns, just need to ensure we have confirmed by [@liam.wentworth|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UMFTKK3RS] on the ticket it is only tagging and a follow (engagement) and that there is no requirement to provide something of value.

Hi [~accountid:6257f823ed2b3e0074fd8114], from article 10.2 and 10.7 of the TVDE law, it would appear that the following are the onboarding requirements in relation to taxi drivers:

# hold a driving licence for more than three years for category B with endorsement in group 2;
# be deemed fit and suitable,
# hold a TVDE driver certificate, issued by IMT, I. P…which, assigns to the interested party a unique TVDE driver registration number, with with which he/she is identified on all electronic platforms;
# have a written contract that constitutes the relationship between the parties (i.e. fleet and taxi driver).

Verification of requirement (2) should be performed through the submission of a valid  certificate of criminal record requested for the purpose of "profession/activity without special law", with function/ category "TVDE driver” and indication that the activity "involves regular contact with minors (Law no. 113/2009)". These certificate should include “no mention” and in particular none of the crimes listed in article 11 TVDE law can be indicated.

These are the requirements at the onboarding. Another question is the verification of these requirements after the this moment. It would appear the TVDE law does not establishes any time periods and I do not see reasons to make a difference between TVDE and taxi. 

However, there is a general principle in TVDE law that Bolt as an electronic platform to block access to drivers that do not comply with all legal requirements when Bolt knows or should have known it (article 14). Having this in mind I think there should be a balance: I do not think this means all these requirements must be reviewed every 3 months, but there should be done at a regular interval: when driving licence or IMT certificate expires for instance? I propose we discuss this matter with [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] in detail to align and reach a balanced and workable solution.

I will send a meeting invite.

[~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18] - The recent decision is Meta provided the below point:

_Para 139: Points (d) and (e) of the first subparagraph of Article 6(1) GDPR must be interpreted as meaning that such processing of personal data cannot, in principle and subject to verification by the referring court, be regarded as necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person, within the meaning of point (d), or for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested In the controller, within the meaning of point (e)._

Since the below would have relied on Article 6(1)(d), I think we need to reconsider this in light of the decision from Meta. The ruling from Meta has effectively ruled out all avenues of legal bases other than (c). With this, I believe even in an emergency situation, we still need to be advised of our legal necessity to provide the data requested and cannot rely on (d) for processing.

h3. :target: *Goal of the project*

The goal of the project was to deliver a revamped learning experience with updated learning materials and units to meet the needs of new joiners supporting the Micromobility business line.  

h3. 🤷‍♀️ *What happened*

We were able to deliver the onboarding and up-skill courses on Monday, 17 July 2023. The road to delivering the courses though looked something like this:

||(/) *What went right*||👎 *What went wrong*||📈 *What we can improve on next time*||
|*Stakeholder communication* - we formed strong and clear communication lines with stakeholders throughout the duration of the project.|*Internal team workflow* - as this was the first major project we worked on in our new work capacity as TD and TPM, we had to clear up our roles and expectations of each other as we went along. Some parts of the process and the flow of tasks were unclear in the beginning.|*Complete a gap analysis* - it will be really lovely to have the opportunity to compile a gap analysis when we next run a similar project|
|*Documentation* - we documented our steps really well and shared/communicated well between the two of us and our stakeholders. 
In addition, we were able to make additional documents available in the form of: 
* Onboarding schedule 
* Instructor led session guidelines
* Onboarding map|*Delayed delivery* - we had initially thought that we would have completed the project by 5 May 2023, but we did not account for other issues such as vacation days, sick leaves, public holidays and the training offsite. Thus, causing us to fall behind on the initial plans.|*Accommodate date changes* - make space or time allowances for tasks so that we are not working on a tight timeline.|
|*Team work* - we worked really well as a pair to deliver the onboarding, considering that this was our first large task|*Simultaneous work demands* - along with the project work, we had ad-hoc tasks that popped up throughout that led to delays as well to the delivery date.| |
|*Dry run* - we were able to complete a full dry run and update the onboarding schedule appropriately before we made the course available|*Hyper focus* - we have two business lines to work on, _Carsharing_ and _Micromobility_. Through-out the duration of the project, we have no time to support Carsharing to the full extent that we would have liked.| |

h3. ⏭️ *Next steps* 

As we have rolled out the training now, the next steps are to: 

* Monitor and track the performance of agents based on the identified success metric 
* Maintain the learning materials to ensure that they are constantly updated
** Along with this, is coming to an a agreement regarding the frequency and process to follow regarding course maintenance

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Market-specific steps*{color}

Reached out to UK, Ireland, and Ukraine CS to discuss the need of their market-specific steps. Answers are added [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1y6ZHkNQzmEt9FkG_VvdfGaAxpC9Do3EXiPAeROJ72zo/edit#gid=1327244539]. 

*Insights:*

* *🇬🇧 UK* market-specific Safety instructions _(if the driver was asking for money to cover a toll fee/congestion charge, the case is not safety-related)_ should apply globally to reduce unnecessary escalations to the Safety team (reducing the AHT, TRT, and avoiding back and forth).
* *🇺🇦 Ukraine* market-specific steps _(if there is no history of rides/successful payments - no refund)_ are reducing the fraud in the market and it was working well so far. This step could be replaced by the “Refund abuse prevention feature” when it goes live.
* *🇮🇪 Ireland* - If the driver submitted PR and left a comment saying that this trip was paid in cash - CS solve the PR with 0 EUR price, not to double charge the rider. Otherwise, if the full price will be confirmed, CS will still have to refund this amount to the rider. Even though I believe it is pretty rare for the drivers to actually submit a PR and this way inform CS that the ride was paid in cash (usually they don’t submit a PR and just send a ticket; Ireland found only 2 examples in the last 2 weeks) we still should have this step globally, to prevent double charges.

_(more detailed information is in_ [_Figma_|https://www.figma.com/file/bTrCcKPOXSz2JILZHTY96N/%F0%9F%9A%97-Rider-paid-cash-for-in-app-payment?type=whiteboard&node-id=60-429&t=f34kSricuBhS4sGP-0]_)_

*Remarks_*
*II. Data Protection Officer*

*Overview: The Data Protection Act enables companies to self-regulate. If we appoint a data protection advisor and notify the FDPIC, we benefit from facilitations in the data protection impact assessment*

* *Voluntary appointment of a data protection officer:*
** Private companies may appoint a data protection advisor pursuant to Art. 10 DPA. These may, but need not, have an employment relationship with the company. It is also advisable not to mix the business of data protection advice with that of other legal advice and representation.
** In contrast to the European GDPR, the appointment of advisors and consultants for private parties is optional. There is a notification requirement for private parties if they wish to make use of the data protection impact assessment exemption (See Chapter: Data Protection Impact Assessment).
** Data protection advisors are internal contact points and also the first point of contact for the FDPIC. If the data protection advisor is not in an employment relationship with the private controller, he or she will regularly have to submit a power of attorney to represent the private controller.
** The duties of the data protection advisor include providing general advice and training to the company on data protection issues. In addition, they assist in the issuance and application of terms of use and data protection regulations. 
** The data protection advisor advises the data controller on data protection issues, but the d*ata controller bears sole responsibility for ensuring that personal data is processed in compliance with data protection requirements.*

* *Exception for high-risk data protection impact assessments:* 
** After conducting a data protection impact assessment, a company may rely solely on internal advice even if the risk remains high, without having to consult the FDPIC in addition, if the data protection advisor also meets the requirements under Article 10(3) FADP: 
*** Data protection advisors must be able to perform their function in a professionally independent manner and are not bound by instructions vis-à-vis the controller. 
*** In principle, he or she should report directly to the management of the controller. 
*** Data protection advisors may not perform any tasks in the company that are incompatible with the function. 
*** The data protection advisor must have the necessary expertise in data protection legislation and also technical standards for data security.
Finally, private data controllers must publish the contact details of their - data protection advisor and report them to the FDPIC via the reporting portal.
*** Further information on the registration of data protection advisors in the FDPIC's reporting portal: In principle, data controllers should report the contact details of their data protection advisors themselves via the portal.
* *Online Portal*
** For the notification, we require a CH login. With a CH login, an account is subsequently created on the FDPIC's reporting portal. Each account is valid for exactly ONE responsible person (company). This account can only be transferred together with the associated login. +*Recommendation:*+

* *Bolt Operations:*{color:#36b37e} *Name a Data Protection Advisor (DPO) when needed:* {color}The DPO team meets the requirements to act as a data protection advisor (Art 10 (3)). The notification would generate the advantage for Bolt that no clarification with the Swiss authority would have to take place after an impact assessment. At the same time, the supervisory authority clarifies that the data protection advisor does not take the place of the controller, so that no additional liabilities arise for the DPO. 
* *Bolt Support CH Sàrl:* {color:#36b37e}*No appointment of a data protection advisor required:*{color} Since the appointment is not mandatory and it is currently not to be assumed that the Swiss subsidiary does not plan and implement any high-risk processing operations as a controller, an appointment can be dispensed with. 

----

*III. Local Representative*

* *Overview:* Art. 14 nDSG contains the requirements for the mandatory designation of a representative in Switzerland. Data controllers must designate a Switzerland representative if the data controller's registered office is located outside of Switzerland and the data controller processes personal data of people who reside in Switzerland. The data processing must meet one of the following requirements:
** The processing is related to the offer of goods and services or the observation of the behavior of individuals in Switzerland.
** It is a case of large-scale processing.
** The processing is carried out on a regular basis.
** The processing involves a {color:#ff5630}*high risk to the personality of the data subjects.*{color}
* *Who can we appoint as a representative in Switzerland?* We can designate natural persons as well as companies or other organizations that have their registered office in Switzerland as representation in Switzerland.
* *Duties of the representative?* Art. 15. DPA regulates the tasks and duties of the representative in Switzerland. 
** Be the *point of contact for data subjects and the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner*. As part of this, the Switzerland Representative may make legally effective statements and receive such statements by proxy.
** Swiss supervisory authorities may require the representative to hold all relevant information necessary to clarify data protection facts. If the Swiss representative does not cooperate sufficiently with the DPA, the latter may impose sanctions.
** The Swiss representative must also maintain a RoPA (activities in Switzerland).Upon request, it shall provide the DPA with the information contained in the inventory.
* *Liability of the representative?* Controllers are also liable if they designate a Swiss representative in accordance with the principles of the nDSG and must accept responsibility for the conduct of their representative. The Swiss representative is not liable himself, at least in the external relationship. If, on the other hand, the Switzerland representative breaches his agreement with the data controller or processor, he may be held liable in the internal relationship depending on the form of the contract.

+*Recommendation:*+

*Overview:* A register of processing activities becomes mandatory. However, the Ordinance to the Act provides for an exception for SMEs whose data processing involves only a low risk of violations of the personality of data subjects. According to Art 12, the controller must keep a register of its processing activities. This obligation as well as the content of the directory coincides with that of Art 30 GDPR.

The Data Protection Act provides for exceptions for companies that employ fewer than 250 employees and whose data processing involves a low risk of violations of the personality of the data subjects.

*V. Data processing agreements and Requirements for Int. Data Transfers*

Art 31 establishes justifications for processing (listing of cases in which the legislator assumes that an legitimate interest of the controller can be considered): One justification is that the data controller is in economic competition with another person and, for this purpose, processes personal data that is not disclosed to third parties. The legislator expressly states that companies that belong to the same group as the data controller are not considered third parties under this provision.

The legislator expressly states that companies that belong to the same group as the data controller are not considered third parties. 

But it is important to specify exactly which legal entities are involved in the transfer (Intragroup agreement) and what role the actors (data controller/processor) have.  

Also the need for standard contractual clauses for countries that do not offer an adequate level of data protection compared to Switzerland must be taken into account.

*VI. Personal liability of the CEO*

With fines of up to 250,000 Swiss francs, the sanction options for data protection violations seem relatively mild at first glance (GDPR: up to 20 million euros). But beware: "Compared to the EU, those responsible in the company can be fined and held liable as private individuals," . And: "Not knowing does not protect from punishment."

* *Which violation is punished and how severely?*
** Articles 60-63 nDSG deal primarily with penal provisions for violations of information and disclosure obligations. There is also no provision for criminal liability for negligent violations of the nDSG. However, an intentional violation can already be assumed as soon as the violation was accepted.
** Pursuant to Art. 60 nDSG, anyone who violates duties to provide information pursuant to Arts. 19 and 21 nDSG, duties to provide information pursuant to Arts. 25-27 nDSG and duties to cooperate in the context of investigations by the FDPIC pursuant to Art. 49 para. 3 nDSG will be punished with a fine of up to CHF 250,000.00.
** Art. 61 nDSG then penalizes three constellations of intentional breaches of due diligence with a fine of up to CHF 250,000.00. Firstly, Art. 61 lit. a nDSG makes non-compliance with the requirements of Art. 16 f. nDSG punishable when exporting data abroad. 
** A duty of care with regard to data security also exists for the person responsible. A more precise standard of care will result from the Federal Council's provisions on data security pursuant to Art. 61 lit. c in conjunction with Art. 8 para. 3 nDSG. Art. 8 para. 3 nDSG.
** The basis for calculating the amount of the fine is Art. 106 para. 3 SCC. Fault and economic performance are taken into account in the calculation. Companies that strive for data protection compliance thus face lower fines. A company-wide data protection strategy with complete logging is beneficial.
* Who is liable for violations of the Data Protection Act?
** As already in the existing DPA, but in contrast to the GDPR, it is not the company that is liable for violations of the nDSG, but the natural person within the company responsible for the violation. However, the [*message on the new DPA (by the Swiss legislator)*|https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/fga/2017/2057/de] clarifies that this is not based on the employee responsible for action, but on the person responsible for the organization. The liability of managers is clarified with the reference to Art. 6 VStrR in Art. 64 nDSG. This is the only way to ensure that persons in management positions are liable for the violations and not the freshly hired employee.
** Exceptionally, according to Art. 64 para. 2 nDSG, companies can also be held directly liable. if a fine of no more than *CHF 50,000.00* comes into consideration and the investigation of the person liable to prosecution according to Art. 6 VStrR appears disproportionate.

{code:sql}with base as (
	select support_case.user_persona
    	, case when support_case.source = 'beehive_outgoing' then 'outgoing' else 'incoming' end as contact_type
    	, case when support_case.escalated_to_agent is null then 'not_escalated' else 'escalated' end as is_escalated_to_agent
    	, issue_keys.issue_key
    	, support_case.id
    	, support_case.order_id
	from ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case as support_case
	left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue_keys_updated as issue_keys
  		on issue_keys.support_case_id = support_case.id
	where support_case.created_date >= date('2023-06-01')
        and support_case.created_date <= date('2023-06-30')
        and support_case.user_persona in ('driver', 'rider')
        and issue_keys.issue_key in ('cancellation_fee_not_received', 'charged_cancellation_fee')
        and support_case.state in ('closed', 'solved')
        and support_case.order_id is not null
),

order_try as (
	select order_id
		, state
		, reject_reason
		, created
		, rank() over(partition by order_id  order by created desc) as rnk
	from ng_public.company_order_try
	where created_date >= date('2023-05-15')
        and created_date <= date('2023-06-30')
),

rider_refund as (
	select case when rr.refund_type='full' then 'no' else 'yes' end as is_bolt_balance_refund_manual
		, rr.refund_amount
		, rr.order_id
		, round((rr.refund_amount/cr.rate),2) as refund_amount_euro
	from ng_public.etl_billing_refund_user_rides as rr
		left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates as cr
			on rr.currency=cr.currency and date(rr.created_date) = date(cr.valid_on)
	where 1=1
		and date(rr.created_date) >= date('2023-06-01')
     	and date(rr.created_date) <= date('2023-06-30')	
     	and rr.refund_comment not in ('CS automaion', 'FRAUD REFUND', 'refund by CS rider compensation')
),

cs_automations as (
	select safr.context_id as support_case_id
 		, safr.created_date
 		, case when sael.result_type = 'rider_compensation' then 'rider_refund' else 'driver_compensation' end as automation_compensation_type
 		, round((cast(sael.compensation_amount as decimal)/cr.rate),2) as compensation_amount_eur
	 from ng_customer_support.support_automations_find_solution_request as safr
 		left join ng_customer_support.support_automations_automated_solution as saas
 			on safr.id = saas.find_solution_request_id 
 		left join ng_customer_support.support_automations_automated_solution_action as saasa 
 			on saas.id = saasa.automated_solution_id
 		left join ng_public.support_actions_exec_log as sael 
 			on saasa.action_run_id = sael.id
 		left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates as cr
			on cr.currency=sael.compensation_currency and sael.created_date = date(cr.valid_on)
	where 1=1
		and sael.result_type is not null
		and safr.order_system = 'taxi'
		and safr.created_date >= date('2023-06-01')
     	and safr.created_date <= date('2023-06-30')
)

select a.state as order_state
 	, a.reject_reason as driver_rejection_reason
 	, c.automation_compensation_type
 	, r.is_bolt_balance_refund_manual
 	, count(b.order_id) as order_count
 	, round(sum(c.compensation_amount_eur), 2) as automation_compensation_sum_eur 
 	, round(sum(r.refund_amount_euro), 2) as manual_refund_sum_eur
from base as b
 	left join order_try as a
 		on a.order_id = b.order_id
 	left join cs_automations as c
 		on cast(b.id as bigint) = cast(c.support_case_id as bigint)
 	left join rider_refund as r
 		on r.order_id = b.order_id
 where 1=1
 	and a.rnk = 1
 	and a.state in ('client_did_not_show')
group by 1,2,3,4{code}

Rider’s account can get suspended due to violating [Bolt Rider Conduct Guidelines|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/]. Suspension can be caused by 3 elements - cancelation ratio, no-show ratio, and average rating. Suspension differs from the regular block and can be checked in _the rider’s profile → More rider options → Rider status (suspended/active)._ The rider can request CS to lift the suspension and that can be considered in these cases: 

* Cancellation - if the reason for cancellations is due to the driver for over half of the cancellations in the last 90 days.
* No show - if there is suspicion that a driver wrongly set the status for a rider.
* Average rating - if ratings are low because of error or bad judgment.
This is expected and confirmed with Polina and Artur. If we think there’s a better way to do it, let’s raise the topic with them.

Hey [~accountid:618d20acfba4d0006ae30dd3] Bolt Business is mainly for customers’ employees, but let's ask [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a]  if there are cases where we allow Bolt Business use by clients’ customers, not employees. Is such an exception possible if the third party who will use BB is clearly identified?

If the Bolt Drive vehicle gets damaged or a driver gets fined by the police, we will primarily request reimbursement from the user (actual driver) under the T&C for Bolt Drive. If the user does not pay, we keep an option to claim costs from the business client, but this comes as a secondary option. In any event, liability cannot be excluded. We cannot indicate in the agreement that a customer is liable because the customer is not a party to Bolt Business agreement, the contract is between Bolt and a business client.

The business client can sign a separate agreement with its customer stating that it will reimburse a business client any costs Bolt may claim from the business client if the damage to Bolt is caused by the customer. But such an agreement is outside of our scope and shall be dealt with by the client and its customer, without Bolt's involvement.

To disclose any information about a person on our platform (i.e. driver/rider/courier/eater), we need to ensure:

* the person requesting the data has authority to request the data,
* they have a legitimate reason/legal basis to request the data, 
* we only release the minimum amount of data they need i.e. we limit it to what is strictly needed to satisfy their purpose and do not include any sensitive/confidential data and data about other individuals,
* we release the data securely, and
* we keep an audit trail of the request and what we sent in response i.e. everything should be recorded in writing and saved in a Beehive ticket. 

In relation to vehicle information, this could relate to an individual (i.e. the owner of the vehicle) and in some countries knowing the registration can be enough to find out more information about a person. So the rules I outlined above apply to vehicle information too and you should loop in my team (by raising a Jira ticket) so we can review the request and confirm if we can disclose.

It always tries to convert the input value into the options set, that in its turn causes the popup to be opened and the last available option to be focused
So the next “Enter“ key hit causes the unselection of the last option and as a result, the last input value is missed
A possible solution is a workout some special flow for such cases on the admin framework side

This type of letter is an official guarantee from the bank to the landlord that even if we don’t pay in time, we still have the means to pay in 3 months time after the termination of the current contract. It does not state that we will have to pay extra, it’s more of a guarantee from a 3rd party (the bank) that we have the means to pay, even if we are late with the last payments.

It is stated in the Romanian Civil Law. I could not find the text in English, but Article 2321 states: 

(1) The letter of guarantee is the irrevocable and unconditional commitment by which a person, called the issuer, undertakes, at the request of a person called the orderer, in consideration of a pre-existing obligation relationship, but independent of it, to pay a sum of money to a third person‚ referred to as the beneficiary, in accordance with the terms of the assumed commitment.

(2) The commitment thus assumed is executed at the first and only request of the beneficiary, if the text of the guarantee letter does not provide otherwise.
(3) The issuer cannot oppose to the beneficiary the exceptions based on the pre-existing obligation ratio to the commitment assumed by the letter of guarantee and cannot be held to pay in case of abuse or obvious fraud.

{noformat}WITH drivers_age AS (
                        SELECT DISTINCT
                            foc.driver_id,
                            min(date_trunc('day', foc.order_created)) as min_fecha
                        FROM ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check as foc
                        WHERE true AND foc.order_created >= DATEADD(year,-1, CURRENT_DATE)
                        GROUP BY 1
                    )
   , count_of_orders AS (
                            SELECT
                                ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
                                COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                                                        THEN etl.order_id
                                                    ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_orders,
                                COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash'
                                                        THEN etl.order_id
                                                    ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_orders
                            FROM
                                ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
                                    JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot
                                        ON ot.city_id = etl.city_id AND etl.order_id = ot.order_id
                            WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides' AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished' AND
                                etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE) AND ot.state = 'finished'
                            GROUP BY 1
                        )
   , count_of_fraud_orders AS (
                                  SELECT
                                      ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
                                      COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                                                              THEN etl.order_id
                                                          ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
                                      COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash'
                                                              THEN etl.order_id
                                                          ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_fraud_orders
                                  FROM
                                      ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
                                          JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co
                                              ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id
                                          JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot
                                              ON ot.city_id = etl.city_id AND etl.order_id = ot.order_id
                                          LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check AS oc
                                              ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
                                          LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
                                          JOIN drivers_age as da ON (ot.driver_id = da.driver_id)
                                  WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides' AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished' AND
                                      etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL AND ot.state = 'finished' AND
                                      ot.price_review_status = 'ok' AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price AND
                                      co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE) AND
                                      ((etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created) <= 7
                                              AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))
                                              OR (etl.country_code = 'ng'
                                                  AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created) <= 7
                                                  AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 100 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30)
                                                  AND ROUND(etl.rider_discount * 1.00 / etl.partner_price, 2) >= 0.45)
                                            -- Profile that doesn't depend on the discount % or the final price in Nigeria (13207 rides in 7 days --> Fraud code in NG has 25K orders and 40% deleted accounts in 7 days, which means 10K fraud orders approx. only for deleted accounts)
                                            OR (
                                                etl.country_code = 'ng'
                                                AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created) <= 1
                                                AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 30 AND oc.pickup_duration <= 50)
                                                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'cash'
                                                AND co.campaign_code is not null AND co.campaign_code <> ''
                                                --AND uu.phone_anonymized = '0del'
                                                )
                                              OR (DATEDIFF(day,da.min_fecha, CURRENT_DATE) < 15 AND oc.pickup_duration <= 20))
                                  GROUP BY 1
                              )

                       etv.company_order__state AS order_sate,
                       CASE WHEN (driver_accepted_lat = company_order__lat AND driver_accepted_lng = company_order__lng
                               AND company_order__campaign_code IS NOT null AND etv.company_order__state = 'finished')
                                THEN true
                            ELSE false END AS is_fraud_order
                   FROM ng_public_spark.etl_search_denormalized_view AS etv
                   WHERE true AND etv.created_date >= dateadd(day,-8, current_date) AND
                       etv.company_order__state = 'finished'
               )
   , drivers_stats AS (
                          SELECT
                              driver_id,
                              count(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_events,
                              count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_fraud_order = true THEN order_id END) AS fraud_events
                          FROM orders AS o
                          WHERE true
                          GROUP BY 1
                      )
   , same_gps_orders as (
                            SELECT DISTINCT
                                o.city_id || ':' || o.order_id AS profile_key,
                                1 AS fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
                            FROM
                                orders AS o
                                    JOIN drivers_stats AS ds ON (o.driver_id = ds.driver_id)
                            WHERE is_fraud_order = true AND (fraud_events >= 3
                                    OR (cast(fraud_events AS double) / cast(total_events AS double)) >= 0.2) AND
                                (cast(fraud_events AS double) / cast(total_events AS double)) >= 0.1 AND
                                o.city_id NOT IN (993, 997, 991, 1167)
                        )
   , final_table as (
                        SELECT
                            profile_key,
                            fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
                        from pick_up_profile_orders
                        UNION
                        SELECT
                            profile_key,
                            fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
                        FROM same_gps_orders
                    )       
                        SELECT DISTINCT 
                        profile_key as KEY,
                        fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
                        FROM final_table
                        {noformat}

For 2 documents I analysed, I see the problem is that PDF has too big page size set - 42 x 56 inch. Regular A4 has 8,26 x 11,68 inch.

I think the easiest workaround is to:

# Get page size with tool like {{pdfinfo}}
# For documents bigger (total page area) than regular A4 - calculate custom, lower DPI. We use 300 DPI now and it works pretty good for A4 (text is not distorted even when document is a small part of the page - attaching a doc - output_regular_pdf_300dpi blurred). The custom DPI would be set to a value for which result JPEG size would be of A4 300DPI JPEG size. For example (42*56)/(8.26*11.68) = 24.38 (ratio of big pdf page area that I analysed to a4 area). Single dimension ratio (DPI is for one dimension) - 24.38^0.5 = 4.94. New DPI - 300DPI / 4.94 = 60DPI. Applying this DPI reduced JPEG size from 40MB to 4MB while not reducing readability.
# Pass calculated DPI to {{pdftoppm}} tool that we use for pdf conversion



We can think of reducing JPEG size further by decreasing DPI or JPEG quality ratio. Currently we set it to 100%.

HI [~accountid:62d68d2a39248e8689eb4c33] 

I would say that Bolt have standard employment contract templates and no additions to the standard text is allowed.

Regarding her question about notice periods you can say that fixed-term employment does not limit use of the regular termination grounds or notice periods mentioned in Labour Law before end of the fixed-term contract if there will be such need. Clause 12.4. of employment contract states that _This Employment Contract may be terminated on the grounds established in the Labour Code of the Republic of Lithuania._ 

Regarding notice periods for fixed-term employment you can refer her to Article 69 of Lithuanian Labour Law where they are regulated and they are dependant from the length of the employment relationships. I have commented this also previously in this ticket:

* If the employment relationship under the fixed-term employment contract lasts longer than one year, the employer must notify the employee in writing about the termination of the employment contract at the end of the term no later than five working days in advance,
* If the employment relationship under the fixed-term employment contract lasts longer than three years, no no later than ten working days in advance. After violating this duty, the employer must pay the employee wages for each day of violation of the deadline, but not more than five or ten working days.

Detailed description of 

_Rebuild connection between Provider app and Timing Backend to support flow with showing ML to provider._


*Status Quo:*


Order Accepted ML end point has 3 variables that describe provider input:
- preparation_time_with_delay_seconds
- preparation_time_initial_seconds
- delayInSeconds

How are this values populated by Timing backend?

*_Case 1. Provider accepted with new time:_*
preparation_time_with_delay_seconds is equal to the value provider has chosen in app
preparation_time_initial_seconds is equal to provider contractual time

delayInSeconds = preparation_time_with_delay_seconds - preparation_time_initial_seconds

*_Case 2. Provider simply accepted:_*

preparation_time_with_delay_seconds is equal to provider contractual time


preparation_time_initial_seconds is equal to provider contractual time

delayInSeconds = 0



*Problem with status quo setup:*

It is designed and only works in case when provider sees contractual time as an order proposed time. In all other cases it leads to non-sense values calculated and propagated to ML endpoint.



*Solution:*

# Fixed flow (changes in *_bold italics)_*:
## *Provider accepted with new time:*
### preparation_time_with_delay_seconds is equal to the value provider has chosen in app
preparation_time_initial_seconds is equal to *_value that was shown to provider_* 
delayInSeconds = preparation_time_with_delay_seconds - preparation_time_initial_seconds
## *Provider simply accepted:*
### preparation_time_with_delay_seconds is equal to the value provider *_has seen and accepted in app_*
preparation_time_initial_seconds is equal to *_value that was shown to provider_* 
delayInSeconds = preparation_time_with_delay_seconds - preparation_time_initial_seconds = 0

2. Make sure that the values that were shown to provider are correctly stored to database

# + 2. together will allow to use ML model with any values initially shown to provider instead of current setup that is bounded to provider contractual values.

3. (optional) Rename variables to less confusing names:

* preparation_time_with_delay_seconds → preparation_time_accepted_by_provider_seconds
* preparation_time_initial_seconds → preparation_time_proposed_to_provider_seconds
* delayInSeconds → provider_added_delay_seconds

In this case, the best option would be to contact the driver about this requirement and ensure he has an appropriate notice in the car and to acquire license as per applicable local laws.

I can see in the notebook that you first read the data using {{sqlContect.sql()}}, then you convert the Spark DataFrame to Pandas using {{toPandas()}} and at the very end, you convert it back to Spark DataFrame to write it to S3.

{{toPandas()}} is the problematic part. It requires all workers to send the data back to the driver node and the driver needs to fit the data in its memory. The driver doesn’t have enough memory, so you get the error. This is not the correct approach though - you shouldn’t send the intermediate data to the driver, but it should be kept as Spark DataFrame all the way from beginning to end. This way the data stays in the workers and the cluster can be scaled up horizontally to account for the growing dataset.

Long story short, you need to rewrite your logic and stick to Spark DataFrame. If you don’t want to do it, for the sake of completing the backfill you can split the data into batches, so the worker is not overfilled. Increasing {{spark.driver.maxResultSize}} is not an option here, because it’s not the proper solution to the problem.

query to match the latest received and answered cases with the compensations

issue found - if the driver has more than 1 compensation added for the same week; a possible solution - to match then smaller ID = earlier created ticket

{code:sql}-- relevant driver compensations with the driver_id
with comp as(
select cda.client_id
	, cda.id
	, rank() over (partition by cda.client_id order by cda.id desc) as comp_rank
	, ic.external_id as driver_id
	, cda.currency 
	, cda.compensation_amount 
	, cda.compensation_fee_type 
	, cda.compensation_fee_subtype 
	, cda.created 
	, cda.admin_user_id 
	, cda.compensation_comment 
	, cda.created_date 
from ng_public.etl_billing_compensation_driver_adjustment as cda
left join ng_public.invoicing_client as ic
	on cda.client_id = ic.id 
where 1=1
	and ic.type = 'Driver'
	and cda.compensation_fee_type not in ('bonus','account_migration')
	and cda.compensation_fee_subtype not in ('fraud_deduction', 'compensation_fuel', 'driver_misconduct', 'ride_overcharge')
),
-- relevant support cases and support case data 
support_case as (
select edasc.id
	, edasc.user_id
	, edasc.created
	, edasc.created_date
	, slo.slo_resolved_at
	, scik.issue_keys
from ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case as edasc
inner join customer_support.support_case_response_time_slo_resolved as slo
	on edasc.id = slo.support_case_id
	and slo.slo_type = 'first_response_time'
	and slo.slo_resolved_at is not null 
left join customer_support.support_case_issue_keys as scik
	on edasc.id = scik.support_case_id
where 1=1
	and edasc.state not in ('draft', 'duplicate')
	and edasc.escalated_to_agent is not null
	and edasc.order_id is not null
),
comp_2 as (
select sc.id as support_case_id
	, rank() over (partition by co.id order by sc.created desc) as case_rank
	, sc.user_id as driver_id
	, sc.created as case_created
	, sc.issue_keys
	, co.comp_rank
	, co.created as comp_created
	, co.currency
	, co.compensation_amount
	, co.compensation_fee_type
	, co.compensation_fee_subtype
	, co.compensation_comment
from support_case as sc
left join comp as co
	on sc.user_id = co.driver_id
	and date_diff('day', date(sc.created_date), date(co.created_date)) < 7 --- probably not needed as the process is new
	and date(sc.created_date) <= date(co.created_date)
	and sc.slo_resolved_at < co.created
where 1=1
order by sc.created_date desc
)
select support_case_id
	, case_rank
	, driver_id
	, case_created
	, issue_keys
	, comp_created
	, currency
	, comp_rank
	, compensation_amount
	, compensation_fee_type
	, compensation_fee_subtype
	, compensation_comment
from comp_2
where 1=1
	and case_rank = comp_rank
limit 100
	{code}
