Hi [~accountid:613ec5968f2ada00692f09d1], I reviewed the blocking rules and the possibility to eliminate settling the payment outside of the platform. I’m sharing my insights with you, please let me know your thoughts and if this is sufficient for proceeding with the article update. 🙏

+*Blocking rules:*+

* *🇹🇭 Thailand, 🇸🇻 El Salvador, 🇭🇳 Honduras, and East Africa* will follow the Global blocking rules, thus these country names should be removed from the market-specific blocking instructions. ✅
* *🇫🇷France, 🇵🇾 Paraguay, 🇪🇸 Spain* will continue following the current market-specific rules since that was their local OPS teams' request, they have many drivers creating fake accounts and doing fake orders, other market-specific reasons such as being supply-caped or cash-heavy market. 🔴

+*Settling the payment outside of the platform:*+

* The part of the process for riders settling the payment with the drivers is already removed and a separate article had to be created, but that is *not needed* and this step should be eliminated for the following reasons:
** 11 markets confirmed, that it is rare for the riders to be interested in paying back to the driver and to ask to be unblocked regarding unpaid rides. 
** In the markets where the global blocking rules are followed, the rider gets permanently blocked after the 3rd unpaid ride, which is an excellent indicator that the rider is willing to violate our rules, so we shouldn’t create the conditions for fraudulent riders to continue not paying for the rides.
** Settling the payment outside of the platform is quite problematic_,_ lacking clear guidelines for various possible outcomes and requiring CS to share the personal information of riders/drivers.
** In most cases, the driver’s compensation is already handled either through automation or by the CS team manually.
** Coordinating payment between riders and drivers outside of our platform is beyond the scope of our services, and supporting such arrangements poses challenges.

Based on the reasons listed above, *rider education & blocking* should remain the only actions toward the rider in this process.

* What are the services being provided under the agreement? Motor insurance/ 3rd party coverage
* What data is being shared between the parties? List and details of drivers on our platform
* Who does the agreement benefit i.e. riders, drivers, our employees? Drivers

Hello [~accountid:641172642cee496759ea7646] , good morning.

Your concern regarding e-signatures in Switzerland makes sense and it is based on the fact that, with Adobe Sign it is not possible to achieve QES (qualified electronic signature) in Switzerland.

QES have the same effects as handwritten signature according to the Swiss Code of Obligations. Note that there are some excepted contracts that expressly require handwritten signature (or QES) by law.

However, other e-signatures are recognised and governed by the *Federal Act on Electronic Signature (ZertES)* and the *Swiss Code of Obligations*, and are legally binding as well:

# Simple electronic signature (SES) – data in electronic form, which is attached to, or logically associated with, other data in electronic form and which aims at authenticating such data.
# Advanced electronic signature (AES) – a SES that is also:
## uniquely linked to its holder;
## capable of identifying its holder;
## created with means which the holder can use under his or her sole control; and
## linked to the associated data in such a way that any subsequent change in the data is detectable.

In conclusion, we are on the safe side in the sense that the e-signatures we are using are expressly recognised in local regulations.

I hope to have clarified the point, if not, please let me know.

Thank you!

Back then we didn’t explore this topic, but maybe the _audit-log chaos test_ initiative is a good pretext to reiterate on this:

# I suppose it would be relatively easy to write an eslint rule that would require the calls to {{audit-log}}’s write endpoints to either be wrapped in {{FireAndForget}} or have a {{fallback}} lambda specified.

Of course the rule could cause some false-positives - I suppose it’d be easy to detect that the call is _directly_ wrapped in {{FireAndForget}}, but not so easy to detect that the call occurs in a method, which in turn is wrapped in {{FireAndForget}}. But I guess we could live with that.

The rule also wouldn’t help with _essential data loss_ problem. But still worth exploring IMO. And once we have such a rule in place, we could try to make it re-usable somehow.

The point of rebooting IOT is to solve cases when where iot isnt working properly, not for the agents to open the doors, when user can’t do it themselves. 
Actually, this should only happen in cases where user is far away from the city, and for some random reason, IOT does not let user open the door or start the car. [~accountid:628dd7169c617b006a6d8f2e] I created a design doc with a new proposal for the reports, in the tech point of view: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4502028529/2023-07+Work+Profile+Report|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4502028529/2023-07+Work+Profile+Report|smart-link] 

Just to recap, this is what we have today

# Reports start only on the 4th day of the month
## This is a workaround because we want all invoices of the month to be in the report and we have an internal SLA of 3 days for doing invoice fiscalizations.
# Reports take 36 hours to finish (around the 5th day of the month)
## We are blocked by the invoice service, once we get the invoice data for every single report during this time it is hard for us to speed up.

The 1st issue is that we wait 72 hours just to start running the reports, once we are waiting for invoices to be fiscalized. If we remove this requirement, it would already be a big win and we would be able to deliver all reports until the 2nd day of the month.

The 2nd issue is that the current solution is not scalable. It already take 36 hours and it can grow exponentially as we start generating more reports, once we will be overloading the invoicing service, requesting the invoicing data on the fly.

In the new solution I am proposing 2 things

# Start storing the data in the WP Database, so we don’t have to query for invoice data when we are generating the report
## This will speed up the process a lot, it is hard to measure but with propose implementation I don’t see why we cannot do everything in ~12 hours.
## The 1st limitation here is that we just receive notifications about invoices that were finished after they were fiscalized, but if we still wait for the 3 days to start the report it would behave the same, just be faster to process.
# Remove the invoice fiscalization limitation
## This is the harder product decision we have to make. Do we really need to wait for invoices to be fiscalized to send the report? Can we make it clear in our terms & conditions that we will report only invoices that were fiscalized?



I am not sure current “wait for 3 days” solution also does not solve all cases. 
Maybe it is possible that we miss this time because of holidays, high load, or even in cases where we have different timezones (reports run in UTC), even thought if we wait for 3 days, they should be very rae.

Hey! 



The timeframe for submitting a claim depends on the type of insurance. For example, for personal accident claims, the timeframe can be stipulated by the insurance provider, however, when it comes to third-party damages it’s not as simple. Civil liability to third parties is regulated by local laws and depends on the specific country’s legislation for this. 

I am not familiar with German civil law, so I asked our insurance broker about the timeframe for third-party liability claims, he should know this. However, our broker company in Germany is unfortunately on collective leave until 08/08. 

(We can also ask our German legal counsels to advise on this.) 

Sufficient to say, that if the claim is submitted within one year from occurring the damage, it’s highly likely that it will be a valid claim.



However, reading the conversation above, even if we delete user accounts (and user data thereof), the historic data related to any trips taken on our platform will (and should!) stay intact. Aside from insurance claims, what if someone commits a crime using our scooters, and the police need the data for investigation? Deleting one’s user account from our platform should not become a tool to protect oneself from legal consequences. 



So to sum up, I see no issues with us sharing the trip information with our insurance provider, especially considering that Bolt has a contractual obligation to hand over that data to the insurance provider (GDPR 6c). See the highlighted part of the contract below, please. 



Best 

Karmel

When we are calculating the courier earnings for a zone, we should consider the following:

* if something is not defined for the zone, then we default to the city settings.
* example for the base rates:
** if city pickup component = 0.5, drop-off component = 0.5 
** if zone pickup component = 0.75, drop-off component is undefined
*** then, when calculating the earnings for a courier in the zone, we consider that pickup component = 0.75 (defined from the zone), drop-off component = 0.5 (from the city)
* example with the multipliers:
** city multiplier for 10:00 - 11:00 for pickup component = 1.1 and for drop-off component = 1.1
** if zone multiplier for 10:00 - 11:00 not defined
*** then when calculating earnings for the zone for 10:00 - 11:00, we consider that multipliers for pickup and drop-off are 1.1 (coming from city settings)
** if zone multiplier for 10:00 - 11:00 is: pickup component = 1.2, drop-off component not defined
*** then when calculating earnings for the zone for 10:00 - 11:00, we consider that multiplier for pickup is 1.2 (coming from zone settings), and for drop-off is 1.1 (from city settings)

I will make a draft of how the KB could look like and hop this helps:

*PT-specific Safety Guidelines* 

Due to reclassification risks, it is very important to understand specific rules related to driver blocking in  PT. 

*Driver Blocking:*

Drivers *will not* get consequentially blocked for *Low- and Moderate Events (Minor cases on Beehive)*, but only educated. The Local Operations team will monitor the quality.

*What if the driver repeats low and moderate events (Minor cases on Beehive :*

* In these cases, *the driver still cannot be blocked*
* The agent should follow all other instructions of the tool (except blocking the driver) 
* The local operations team is responsible for monitoring the frequency of events by a driver and passing feedback to the Fleet owner. 

*When is blocking a driver allowed :*

Drivers can only get Consequentially blocked for Significant and high-risk cases (Severe and Critical on Beehive) 

*The Tool will replace Driver Block with Car Block when the event is related to car safety*. (Will be flagged every time that the Agent fills Global Event Assessment Tool).

* Driver in Vehicle Accident Causing Injury or Structural Damage
* Driver in Vehicle Accident Resulting in any Cosmetic Damage
* Not Fit for Purpose Vehicle Use

*NB*

* When the tool suggests that the vehicle will be blocked instead of the driver, no other action is required from CS agents.
* The operations team will receive a notification and block the vehicle.
* The agent should follow the rest of the instructions on the tool
* The agent will not have to unblock the vehicle after doing their Safety investigation, as this will be done by the operations team.

Hello Martyna, thank you for following up on this! To give more information on the questions raised:

# Blocking permissions are restricted to Tier-2 only on request of the local OPS team. In the past, we have come across cases of accidental blocks on wrong accounts or agents lifting OPS blocks related to expired documents or similar, critical to our compliance. While this is an agent behaviour issue, as the market is highly regulated, even the smallest margin of error could have severe implications.
# No actions required from Tier-1 after the ticket is closed. This is simply a prompt for Tier-2 to de-escalate the ticket if any questions out of Tier-2 scope arise after the block is placed. This logic, as well as the general logic for Tier-2 placing blocks, is already in place in the [UK escalation guidelines|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7076414532114#additional-information-adding-and-removing-cs-blocks] - Tier-1 take all the actions necessary per the process, advise the user, and escalate to Tier-2 only for the purpose of lifting/placing a block.
# With regard to further examples - I believe [~accountid:5cde6b461b6dba0dc52c2103] would be best suited to support. To my knowledge, we have only seen one such incident, the one linked to the case. As, once again, drivers carrying out trips on unvetted vehicles is a critical compliance issue, in this case it’s important to introduce process changes prior to us seeing more cases like this.

Thank you!

*Suggested process update*

*Step 1: Check for Fraudulent Patterns*

* The estimated distance and actual driven distance don’t match (the difference is above 20 km).
* The destination entered and ride finish locations are different.
* Drastic overcharge on a short trip.
* In the "Route points" tab on the order in Admin, check for "isSpeedDeltaTooFast" and "isDistanceDeltaTooBig" flags, indicating illogical speed calculations.
* Pay attention to multiple log-ins on the *Driver's Devices* during a single ride, as it may suggest possible fraudulent activities.

*Step 4 (Follow-up on the Report): GPS Spoofing*

* If automation was applied, inform the rider accordingly.
* If automation wasn't applied, compensate the overcharged amount with the Driver as a refund actor (deduct the refund amount from the driver’s earnings) and inform the rider accordingly.
* For cash trips, compensate the rider following your market rules.

*Step 5: Log the Report*

* If not already added, select the correct order from the Bolt Admin Panel. The report about the driver's behavior is now collected automatically.

*Step 6: Action the Report*

* If it's an isolated case, leave a comment on the order and close the ticket.
* If the driver has a history of multiple GPS overcharges, collect the cases and create an SD ticket to the Fraud team for updating and optimizing the rules if needed.
* *Note*: Do not apply any manual blockings to the driver account.

I see some clarification is needed here. If the accident happens outside of the Bolt platform then it’s not considered a safety incident. We have no authority to investigate the driver’s personal life or ask for his explanation for something that happened outside of our platform. 

But we as Bolt, however, have a responsibility to make sure the driver is using a car that meets all the vehicle requirements and is fit for purpose. We also need to make sure that the driver wouldn’t go and start driving with a different car (like in this case the driver had a courtesy car from his insurance provider and he thought sending us the documents through the app would be sufficient).
